correctness.rationale: In normalized time, integrating the linear equations for X as a function of Y gives X_L=e^{-Y}(F(Y)-kappa) and X_R=(1/2)e^{-2Y}(F(Y)^2-lambda), with F(y)=(y-1)e^y. Because F'=y e^y and F(0)=-1, there are exactly two crossing roots p<0<q<1 for -1<kappa<0. Between them F<kappa<0, so the kappa and lambda=kappa^2 arcs are in their correct half-planes. At p both horizontal components are positive and at q both are negative; other roots above 1 are not transverse crossings of the periodic component. A transverse cycle must have crossings of each of these two types, since Y is strictly monotone in each zone; each flight takes q-p, and neither can close earlier. Thus the least normalized period is 2(q-p). Branch inversion yields the stated W difference and p'<0<q' gives strict growth. At the inner end the signed square root of 2(F(y)+1) is analytic with derivative 1 at zero, so its inverse at oppositely signed arguments gives q-p=2 sqrt(2(kappa+1))+O((kappa+1)^{3/2}). At the outer end set u=-W_{-1}(kappa/e); then u-log u=L, u tends to infinity, and u/L tends to 1, so u=L+log L+o(1), while W_0 tends to zero. This gives the sharp stated divergence at an unbounded boundary, not a finite saddle. The original tau-time scaling is division by delta. The assessment is analytic; no independent numerical spot checks were necessary or run.
residual_risks: The normalized law is only for the delta>0 canonical family and transverse cycles; the origin and outer limiting boundary are not nontrivial finite cycles.
The two vector fields on X=0 are interpreted by transverse crossing on the annulus. No assertion is made about sliding, stability, or the delta=0 family.
